Creates the team user. Supply either password or activation_email; activation_email=1 sends an email allowing the team user to set a password. The client does not enforce this cross-parameter condition or send a message independently. Password is sensitive and stays in the form POST body.

roles uses one comma-separated wire field; this operation rejects the singular role parameter. A team user without roles cannot use any features. Adding a team user can grant team owner level privileges. notes must not contain private information and is documented with a 100-character maximum.

expire_date is an integer Unix Epoch Time or a string offset such as 120days. When returned, the response is the resulting Unix timestamp. Optional service flags default to 0 upstream; Web Disk permissions default to rw. Email quota is a string in MB; 0 or unlimited means unlimited and the system maximum still applies. Omitting quota retains the defined system value.

A subaccount is always created, without service subaccounts by default. FTP and Web Disk home directories are relative to the cPanel account home. The FTP directory must exist; the source says its homedir parameter is required if services.ftp.homedir is enabled, a self-referential condition retained without inventing client validation. Web Disk homedir is required when Web Disk is enabled. Web Disk private selects 0700 versus public 0755. Digest authentication is discouraged and only documented for compatibility on certain Windows clients with self-signed cpsrvd/cpdavd certificates.

Reviewed upstream source on cPanel 11.138.0.19 returns null when expire_date is omitted and an expiration timestamp when supplied. Canonical integer-string timestamps normalize to int within PHP's integer range; explicit null stays null and absent data is a payload mismatch. Team was unavailable on that server, so this correction has source and offline replay evidence only.

Client lists preserve order, duplicates, empty string items and all other bytes, and reject empty, keyed or nonstring lists and items containing a comma before dispatch. Scalars retain commas, percent escapes and empty strings without parsing or pre-encoding. Optional null omits the field; an empty list never means omission. Collection arguments are trace-protected without changing transport or classifying the field as a semantic secret.
